intro: IELTS 6.0 darajasida bitta passage'da odatda ikki yoki uch xil savol turi keladi. Passage 1 da eng ko'p uchraydigan juftlik — TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN va jadval (table) to'ldirish.

Birinchi qadam — XARITA. Matnni o'qishdan oldin ikkala savol guruhiga 1 daqiqa ko'z yugurtiring va har guruh matnning qaysi qismiga tegishli ekanini taxmin qiling. Student's Book'da 1–6 savollar Avstraliya qadriyatlari haqida, 7–13 esa madaniyat shokining to'rt bosqichi haqida.
Jadval sarlavhasi va ustun nomlari qaysi xatboshilarni o'qish kerakligini aytadi: "THE STAGES OF CULTURE SHOCK" — faqat bosqichlar tasvirlangan xatboshilar. Butun matnni qayta o'qish shart emas.

T/F/NG: savoldagi kalit so'zni (ism, raqam, noyob so'z) belgilang va matndan toping. Ma'no bir xil — TRUE; matn qarshisini aytadi — FALSE; matnda bu ma'lumot yo'q — NOT GIVEN. Savollar matn tartibida keladi.
NOT GIVEN tuzog'i: mavzu matnda bor, lekin aynan savoldagi da'vo yo'q. Masalan, matnda "circumstances" so'zi bor, lekin "ustozlar o'quvchining shaxsiy hayotiga qiziqadi" degan gap yo'q.

Jadval: avval so'z chegarasini o'qing (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS — ikki so'zdan oshmasin), keyin har bo'shliq uchun so'z turini aniqlang (ot, sifat, fe'l, raqam). Javob matndan aynan ko'chiriladi, imlosi o'zgartirilmaydi.
Vaqt: Passage 1 ga 17–20 daqiqa. Qiyin savolda 2 daqiqadan ko'p to'xtamang — belgilab, keyingi guruhga o'ting va oxirida qayting.
presentation: Qaysi guruhdan boshlayman?
Odatda tartib bilan: avval 1–6, keyin 7–13. Lekin boshlashdan oldin ikkalasiga ham qarab chiqing.
FALSE va NOT GIVEN ni qanday ajrataman?
FALSE — matn qarshi ma'lumot beradi (isbot gap bor). NOT GIVEN — isbot gap umuman yo'q.
Savoldagi so'z matnda bor. Demak TRUE-mi?
Yo'q. So'z bir xil bo'lishi ma'no bir xil degani emas. Butun da'voni tekshiring.
Jadvaldagi javoblar ham tartibdami?
Odatda (USUALLY) ha — jadval qatorlari matn tartibida boradi.
"problem-solving skills" necha so'z?
Ikki so'z: chiziqcha bilan yozilgan so'z bitta so'z hisoblanadi.
Javobni o'z so'zim bilan yozsam bo'ladimi?
Yo'q. Jadvalga faqat matndagi so'z, aynan o'sha shaklda yoziladi.
notes: Bu kursning asosiy yangiligi — savol turlarining KOMBINATSIYASI. 5.0 da har savol turini alohida o'rgandik; endi bitta passage'da ularni birga yechamiz.
Har javobdan keyin ikki savol bering: "isbot qaysi gapda?" va "savoldagi qaysi so'z matnda qanday aytilgan?"
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: xaritani 1 daqiqada chizib, 1–6 va 7–13 matnning qaysi xatboshilariga to'g'ri kelishini oldindan aytish.

class_ex.title: Ko'k xatboshi: uchta savol (SB, 4-mashq)
class_ex.instr: Faqat matnning birinchi (ko'k) xatboshisini o'qing. Har javob uchun isbot gapni ayting.
items: Culture shock affects most people who spend time living in another country.
Culture shock affects certain types of people more quickly than others.
Culture shock only affects how people feel.
why: "Almost everyone who studies, lives or works abroad has problems". "Most people" = "almost everyone".
Kimga tezroq ta'sir qilishi haqida hech narsa yo'q. Mavzu bor, da'vo yo'q — NOT GIVEN.
Ta'rifda "physical and emotional discomfort" — faqat his-tuyg'u emas, jismoniy ham. "Only" so'zi javobni FALSE qiladi.
class_ex.note: Uchinchi savoldagi "only" ni doskada doiraga oling: cheklovchi so'zlar ko'pincha FALSE ga olib keladi.

class_ex.title: Bo'shliq turini oldindan aytish (SB, 6-mashq)
class_ex.instr: 7–13 savollarga javob bermasdan, har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini ayting.
items: 7 — 1-bosqichning nomi
8 — "They notice the ___ between different nationalities"
9 — "for up to ___"
10 — "lose the ___ they had at the beginning"
11 — "understand some ___ which they had not previously observed"
12 — "They learn ___ for dealing with difficulties"
13 — 4-bosqichning nomi
why: Jadvalda 2- va 3-bosqich nomlari berilgan — 1- va 4-bosqich nomi matndan topiladi.
"the ___ between" — orasidagi narsa: farq yoki o'xshashlik; "notice the" dan keyin ot.
"up to" dan keyin vaqt: kun, hafta, oy.
"lose the ___ they had" — boshida bor bo'lgan narsa, ya'ni kayfiyat yoki his.
"some ___ which" — sanaladigan ot ko'plikda.
"learn ___ for dealing with" — ko'nikma yoki usul.
Oxirgi bosqich nomi — oxirgi xatboshida.

tasks.title: Questions 1–6
tasks.type: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: TRUE — matn xuddi shu ma'noni aytadi; FALSE — matn qarshisini aytadi; NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqida ma'lumot yo'q. Tagiga chizilgan so'zlar (teachers, circumstances, first names, study all the time, financial, older) matnda joyni topishga yordam beradi.
items: Australian teachers will suggest alternatives to students rather than offer one solution.
In Australia, teachers will show interest in students' personal circumstances.
Australians use people's first names so that everyone feels their status is similar.
Students who study all the time may receive positive comments from their colleagues.
It is acceptable to discuss financial issues with people you do not know well.
Younger Australians tend to be friendlier than older Australians.
why: "Will not tell students what to do, but will give them a number of options". "Suggest alternatives" = "give a number of options".
"Circumstances" so'zi matnda bor, lekin ustozlarning qiziqishi haqida emas — o'quvchi o'zi eng yaxshi yo'lni tanlashi haqida. Tuzoq: so'z bor, da'vo yo'q.
"Uncomfortable with differences in status ... treating everyone equally. An illustration of this is that most adult Australians call each other by their first names".
"Some students may be critical of others who they perceive as doing nothing but study". "Positive comments" — "critical" ning teskarisi.
"Financial matters ... are only discussed with close friends". Notanish odam bilan — qabul qilinmaydi.
Yosh va keksa avstraliyaliklarning do'stonaligi solishtirilmaydi. "Older people" faqat yoshini so'rash odobsizligi haqida.
tasks.note: 2- va 6-savol — darsning asosiy NOT GIVEN namunasi. O'quvchi "isbot gapni ko'rsat" deganda ko'rsata olmasa, javob NOT GIVEN.

readings.title: Practice 1: Settling in
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 1 darajasi)
text: Every September, thousands of students arrive at universities in countries where they have never lived before. For many of them, the first few weeks are the hardest part of their entire degree. A survey carried out in 2019 found that nearly two thirds of first-year international students felt lonely during their first term, although most said that the feeling had faded by the end of the year.

Universities have responded by creating a range of support services. The most common is the 'welcome week', a programme of events that takes place before classes begin. New arrivals are met at the airport, shown around the campus and given help with practical tasks such as opening a bank account and registering with a doctor. Attendance is not compulsory, but staff report that students who miss it tend to ask for help later, and often with more serious problems.

Another popular idea is the buddy scheme, in which each newcomer is paired with a student who has already completed a year at the university. The buddy is not a teacher or a counsellor; their role is simply to answer everyday questions and to introduce the newcomer to other people. At one university in the north of England, where the scheme was introduced in 2008, buddies receive a short training course but no payment.

Language can be a barrier even for students with high test scores. Academic English is very different from the English of textbooks, and many students are surprised by the speed of lectures and the amount of informal vocabulary they hear. For this reason, most universities offer free academic writing workshops, which are usually held in the evening so that they do not clash with lectures.

Finally, counselling services have expanded. In the past, students tended to visit a counsellor only when they were in serious difficulty. Today, many universities encourage early contact, and some run group sessions in which students discuss homesickness openly. According to counsellors, simply hearing that others share the same feelings is often enough to reduce anxiety.

readings.title: Practice 2: Living with a host family
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 1 darajasi)
text: For many language students, a host family is their first real contact with a new culture. Instead of living in a student residence, the student rents a room in an ordinary family home, usually with meals included. Agencies that arrange these stays say that demand has doubled in the last decade, mainly from students aged between sixteen and twenty-five.

The arrangement has obvious advantages. Students hear the language every day, often in situations that no classroom can reproduce, such as family arguments or conversations about television programmes. Research by one large network of language schools suggests that students who live with families make faster progress in speaking than those in residences, although there was no difference in their writing scores.

However, the experience is not always easy. The most common complaint concerns food. Meal times vary greatly between cultures, and a student who is used to eating dinner at nine in the evening may find that their host family eats at six. Portions, too, can come as a surprise, in both directions.

A second area of difficulty is house rules. Many families expect guests to tell them if they will be home late, to limit the length of their showers and to keep their room tidy. Students often see these rules as a sign that they are not trusted, while families see them simply as normal behaviour in a shared home.

Agencies recommend that both sides discuss their expectations on the first evening. Some provide a written checklist covering meals, visitors, laundry and the use of the kitchen. Where problems continue, the student can ask to move to another family, but agencies report that fewer than one in ten stays end early.

readings.title: Practice 3 (uyga): Coming home — reverse culture shock
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 1 darajasi), uy vazifasi
text: Most people expect to find life abroad difficult. Far fewer expect to struggle when they return home. Yet psychologists say that 'reverse culture shock' is common among students, aid workers and business people who have spent more than six months overseas, and that it can be more upsetting than the original experience because it is so unexpected.

The problem is that both the traveller and their home have changed. Friends have new jobs and new interests, prices have risen, and even the traveller's own language may contain new expressions. Meanwhile, the returnee has developed different habits and opinions. A study of 300 Japanese employees returning from postings in the United States found that almost half felt they no longer fitted in at their company.

Researchers usually describe reverse culture shock in three stages. The first is sometimes called 'disengagement'. It begins before the journey home, when the traveller starts saying goodbye and thinking about what they will miss. Many people report feeling tired and emotional during this period.

The second stage, the 'initial euphoria', follows arrival. Returnees enjoy seeing their family and eating familiar food, and this pleasure may last for a few days. It ends when they realise that other people are only briefly interested in their stories. A former volunteer who had worked in Ghana described how her friends 'listened for about five minutes and then changed the subject'.

The third stage, 'irritability and hostility', is the hardest. Returnees may criticise their own country and feel lonely even among old friends. Experts advise them to join groups of people who have also lived abroad and to keep using the skills they gained overseas, such as a foreign language. With time, most reach a final balance in which they value both cultures.

intro: Section 1 — ikki kishi o'rtasidagi kundalik suhbat (klubga yozilish, so'rovnoma, bron qilish). Faqat shu section'da boshida misol (example) beriladi. 6.0 darajasida Section 1 odatda ikki savol turidan iborat: forma yoki note completion va multiple choice.

Tayyorlanish vaqti qisqa, shuning uchun uni ikkiga bo'ling. Forma uchun: har bo'shliqqa qanday ma'lumot kerak — millat, raqam, ism, kasb, qiziqish. MCQ uchun: har savolning kalit g'oyasini tagiga chizing ("problem for Jenny", "members NOW", "how often", "most frequent", "main purpose").
Ism va manzillar ko'pincha harflab aytiladi: "F-double O" = FOO. Raqamlarda "oh" = 0, "double" = ikki marta. Raqamni har doim son bilan yozing, so'z bilan emas.

TUZOQ (distractor): gapiruvchi avval bir ma'lumotni aytadi, keyin boshqasini beradi yoki tuzatadi. Jenny "Kuala Lumpur" va "United States" ni aytadi, lekin formada so'ralgan millat — "Malaysian". Birinchi eshitgan so'zni darhol yozmang — gap oxirigacha tinglang.

MCQ: uch variantning hammasi odatda audioda eshitiladi. To'g'risi — savoldagi shartga mos kelgani. "How many members does the club have NOW?" — 30 (o'tgan yil), 50 (hozir), 80 (keyingi yil). Kalit so'z: "currently" = now.
Javob savoldagi so'z bilan emas, paraphrase bilan keladi: "once every two weeks" = "every second Thursday"; "most frequent" = "the usual thing".
Oxirida transfer: imlo, ko'plik "-s", so'z chegarasi (ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER) — shu uch narsa ko'p ball olib qo'yadi.
formulas: Birinchi so'z har doim javob emas
presentation: Harflashda adashib qoldim. Nima qilaman?
Eshitganingizni yozing va keyingi savolga o'ting. To'xtab qolsangiz, keyingi javob ham o'tib ketadi.
"Double" nima degani?
Harf yoki raqam ikki marta: "double O" = OO, "double seven" = 77.
Formada "Road" yozilgan. Men ham yozamanmi?
Yo'q. Formada bor so'zni takrorlamang — faqat bo'shliqqa kerak qismni yozing ("13 Anglesea").
MCQ da uchala variant ham eshitildi.
Bu normal. Savoldagi shartni qayta o'qing: hozirmi, eng ko'pmi, asosiy maqsadmi?
Raqamni so'z bilan yozsam bo'ladimi?
Bo'ladi, lekin xato ehtimoli ko'p. Son bilan yozing: 040 422 9160.
Forma va MCQ orasida pauza bo'ladimi?
Ha, odatda qisqa pauza va yangi ko'rsatma. Shu paytda Q6–10 ni yana bir marta ko'zdan kechiring.
notes: 5.0 da forma va MCQ ni alohida o'rgangan edik. Endi ular bitta section'da ketma-ket keladi — o'tish paytida adashmaslik asosiy ko'nikma.
Tekshiruvda har javobdan keyin skriptdan aynan o'sha gapni ekranga chiqaring va tuzoq gapni boshqa rang bilan ko'rsating.
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: Workbook audiosini 1.25 tezlikda tinglash yoki skriptni yopib, tuzoq gaplarni xotiradan aytish.

every second Thursday = once every two weeks
Harflashni oxirigacha tinglash kerak: O-N, E-N emas

how: CORE — forma va so'rovnomalarda keladigan so'zlar; STRONG — shahar hayotini baholash; SUPER — suhbatdagi paraphrase iboralari.
Har o'quvchi o'z ma'lumotlari bilan mini-forma to'ldiradi va sherigiga harflab aytadi.

why: "Double O" — ikki marta O.
Uzun nomda harflarni guruhlab yozing: A-N-G / L-E-S / E-A.
"Oh" — nol. Telefon raqami guruhlab aytiladi: 3 + 3 + 4.

class_ex.instr: Ustoz gapni o'qiydi. O'quvchilar savolga javob beradi va tuzoqni aytadi.
items: "Last year we had 30 members, currently about 50, and next year we'll have about 80." — How many members now?
"I was born in Kuala Lumpur, but I lived in the United States for a couple of years." — Nationality?
"At the moment I'm doing a temporary job with a company — I'm an economist, in fact." — Occupation?

"We meet every second Thursday, so a couple of times a month." — How often?
why: "Currently" = now. 30 va 80 — tuzoq.
Shahar va boshqa davlat — tuzoq; millat keyingi gapda keladi: "So you're Malaysian?"
"Temporary job with a company" — kasb emas, ish joyi.
"What I like best" — eng yoqtirgani. "Singing" formada allaqachon bor.
"Every second" = har ikkinchi, ya'ni ikki haftada bir.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Javob paraphrase bilan keladi. Variantdagi so'z eshitilgani uchun uni tanlamang.
items: 6 According to Don, what might be a problem for Jenny? A) her accent B) talking to her colleagues C) understanding local people
7 How many members does the club have now? A) 30 B) 50 C) 80
8 How often does the club meet? A) once a week B) once every two weeks C) once a month
9 What is the club's most frequent type of activity? A) a talk B) a visit C) a meal
10 The main purpose of the club is to help members to A) meet Australians. B) learn about life in Australia. C) enjoy themselves together.
why: "You might find some of our Australian slang more difficult to understand". A — tuzoq: aksenti "really nice"; B — "I don't suppose you have any communication problems in the office".
"Currently about 50 members". 30 — o'tgan yil, 80 — keyingi yil.
"Every second Thursday in fact, so a couple of times a month". A tuzoq — "Thursday" so'zi har hafta degan fikr beradi; C — "a couple of times" ikki marta.
"The usual thing is for one of the members to give a little presentation". "Most frequent" = "the usual thing"; presentation = talk. B va C — "from time to time".
"The main point of the club is to give people like you the chance to mix in more with people from this country". "Main purpose" = "main point"; "people from this country" = Australians.
tasks.note: 6-savol — darsning eng yaxshi misoli: variantlarning uchalasi ham audioda eshitiladi (accent, office, slang). Faqat bittasi "problem" deb aytiladi.

items: 6 What does the man say about public transport? A) He doesn't like using it. B) He seldom uses it. C) He has stopped using it.
7 What does the man say about sport in the city? A) Some facilities are better than others. B) He intends to do more of it in the future. C) Someone recommended a place to him before he came.
8 What does the man say about entertainment? A) He doesn't have much time for it. B) There is a very wide range of it. C) It is the best aspect of life in the city.

why: "When I've used it, it's been fine, but I don't use it all that often. I cycle to work". "Seldom" = "not all that often". A — tuzoq: "it's been fine".
"A friend back home who'd lived here for a while told me about it" — kriket klubini oldindan tavsiya qilgan. A — u hamma sharoitni maqtaydi.
"There are so many things to choose from". A — tuzoq: "I don't think I'll have time to go everywhere" — vaqt yetmasligi emas, joy ko'pligi haqida.
"I was expecting a crowded city with litter ... actually it's not at all bad". Kutganidan kam.
"I don't know how common that sort of thing is here". B — tuzoq: hamkasbining mashinasi o'g'irlangan, lekin u "nothing's happened to me so far" deydi.

listenings.title: Jony Academy mashqi: Riverside Sports Centre — membership (Q1–10)
intro: Ustoz skriptni bir marta, oddiy tezlikda o'qiydi (ikki ovoz: RECEPTIONIST va AZIZ). O'quvchilar avval 30 soniya formani va Q6–10 ni o'qiydi.
Har savolda bitta tuzoq bor: tuzatilgan raqam, avval aytilgan variant, "used to" yoki "normally". Tekshiruvda o'quvchi tuzoqni ham aytishi kerak.
transcript: RECEPTIONIST: Good morning, Riverside Sports Centre. How can I help you?
AZIZ: Hi. I'd like to become a member, please. I've just started at the university.
RECEPTIONIST: Great. Let me open a form. Can I take your surname first?
AZIZ: It's Karimov. K-A-R-I-M-O-V.
RECEPTIONIST: And your first name?
AZIZ: Aziz. A-Z-I-Z.
RECEPTIONIST: Thank you. And your address here in the city?
AZIZ: I'm in student accommodation at the moment. It's Flat 6, 29 Harbour Street. Oh, sorry — not 29. It's 92. Ninety-two Harbour Street.
RECEPTIONIST: 92 Harbour Street. And a phone number?
AZIZ: My mobile is oh-seven-seven-three-one, four-eight-two, nine-five-oh.
RECEPTIONIST: 07731 482 950. Now, which type of membership would you like? We have full, off-peak and student.
AZIZ: Hmm. My classes finish at four every day, so off-peak might suit me... but does the student one include the pool?
RECEPTIONIST: Yes, it does. Off-peak doesn't.
AZIZ: Then student, please. I definitely want to swim.
RECEPTIONIST: Fine. Do you have any medical conditions we should know about?
AZIZ: I hurt my knee playing football last year, but that's completely fine now. I do have asthma, though, so I always carry an inhaler.
RECEPTIONIST: Thanks, I'll note that. And how did you first hear about us?
AZIZ: A classmate recommended you last week — but actually, the first time I heard about the centre was from a poster in the library.

RECEPTIONIST: Good, the posters are working then! Now, let me tell you a bit about the centre. The gym is open every day from seven until ten. A lot of people think it's crowded in the evenings, but in fact it's quietest after eight. And from next month you'll see brand-new running machines and bikes — the old ones are being replaced.
AZIZ: Great. And are there swimming lessons for adults?
RECEPTIONIST: Yes. They used to be on Tuesday mornings, but we've moved them to Thursday evenings, which suits more people. The weekend lessons are for children only.
AZIZ: OK. Is there anything I need to bring to my first gym session?
RECEPTIONIST: Just a padlock for your locker. We'll take your photo here today, and the membership card is printed while you wait, so you'll have it already.
AZIZ: And how much is the student membership?
RECEPTIONIST: Full membership is twenty-five pounds a month. Student membership is normally twenty-two, but this month we have a special offer: eighteen pounds a month for the first three months.
AZIZ: Perfect.
RECEPTIONIST: Just one more question for our survey — what's your main reason for joining? Are you training for a competition?
AZIZ: No, nothing like that. It helps with stress, of course, but mainly I want to meet people. I don't know anyone in the city yet.
RECEPTIONIST: Well, you've come to the right place. Welcome to Riverside!

tasks.instr: Uchala variant ham eshitiladi. "Used to", "normally", "a lot of people think" — tuzoq belgilari.
items: 6 What does the receptionist say about the gym? A) It is crowded in the evenings. B) It closes early on Mondays. C) It will have new equipment soon.
7 Swimming lessons for adults are now on A) Tuesday mornings. B) Thursday evenings. C) weekends.
8 What should Aziz bring to his first gym session? A) a photo B) a padlock C) his membership card
9 How much will Aziz pay per month at first? A) £18 B) £22 C) £25
10 What is Aziz's main reason for joining? A) to prepare for a competition B) to meet people C) to reduce stress
why: "From next month you'll see brand-new running machines and bikes". A — tuzoq: "a lot of people think it's crowded ... but in fact it's quietest after eight". B haqida gap yo'q.
"We've moved them to Thursday evenings". A — "used to be"; C — faqat bolalar uchun.
"Just a padlock for your locker". Rasm shu yerda olinadi, karta darhol chop etiladi.
"Eighteen pounds a month for the first three months". 22 — "normally", 25 — full membership.
"Mainly I want to meet people". C — tuzoq: "it helps with stress, of course", lekin asosiy sabab emas; A — "nothing like that".
tasks.note: Tekshiruvda har savol uchun ikki narsani so'rang: to'g'ri javob gapi va tuzoq gapi. Bu Section 1 dagi eng muhim ko'nikma.

homework_intro: Bugun Section 1 da ikki savol turini ketma-ket yechdik: avval forma, keyin multiple choice. Eng ko'p ball ikki joyda yo'qoladi — harflash va tuzoq gaplarda.

Birinchi vazifa — ovozli normativ: ismingiz, familiyangiz, manzilingiz, telefon raqamingiz va kasbingiz (yoki o'qish joyingiz) haqida 5 gapni ingliz tilida ayting va har nomni harflab bering. Ovozli xabarni guruhga yuboring.

Ikkinchi vazifa — sherigingiz bilan "klubga yozilish" suhbati: biringiz Don, biringiz Jenny bo'lasiz. Forma savollarini o'zingiz tuzing va bir-biringizning javobingizni yozib oling (Student's Book, 6-mashq).
Uchinchi vazifa — xatolar daftari: bugungi har xato javobni yozing va sababini belgilang — imlo, raqam, tuzoq yoki paraphrase.

intro: Passage 2 da ko'p uchraydigan juftlik — Matching headings (xatboshiga sarlavha tanlash) va "Choose TWO letters" (beshta variantdan ikkitasini tanlash). 5.0 da ikkala turni alohida o'rgandik; endi ularni bitta passage'da birga yechamiz.

Sarlavhalar topshirig'i imtihonda matndan OLDIN keladi. Shuning uchun birinchi bo'lib sarlavhalarni yeching: bu matnni xatboshima-xatboshi o'qib chiqishga majbur qiladi va oxirida butun passage'ning xaritasi qo'lingizda bo'ladi.

XARITA usuli: har xatboshining yoniga 3–4 so'zlik asosiy g'oyani yozing ("B — organik fermerlik tavsifi", "G — boy va kambag'al davlatlar"). TWO letters savoliga o'tganda shu xaritaga qarab kerakli xatboshini 10 soniyada topasiz.

Sarlavha — xatboshining ASOSIY g'oyasi, bitta gapi emas. Tuzoq: sarlavhadagi so'z xatboshidagi bitta tafsilotga mos keladi ("taste" so'zi D da bor, lekin vi "Testing the taste of organic food" D ning sarlavhasi emas). Xatboshining birinchi va oxirgi gapini diqqat bilan o'qing, lekin o'rtasini ham tashlab ketmang.

Sarlavhalar soni xatboshilardan ko'p (masalan, 9 ta sarlavha, 7 ta xatbosh) — 2 tasi ortiqcha. Har sarlavha faqat bir marta ishlatiladi. Misol (example) sifatida berilgan sarlavhani ro'yxatdan darhol o'chiring.

TWO letters: savoldagi kalit g'oyani belgilang ("negative aspects", "nutritional content"). Javob bitta xatboshida yoki bir necha xatboshida bo'lishi mumkin. Har variantni alohida tekshiring: matnda BOR, TESKARI aytilgan, AYTILMAGAN yoki matnda bor, lekin SAVOLGA tegishli emas.
TWO letters savollari matn tartibida kelishi shart emas, lekin odatda har juftlik matnning bir qismiga tegishli. Vaqt: Passage 2 ga 20 daqiqa — sarlavhalarga 10–11 daqiqa, uch juftlikka 8–9 daqiqa.
formulas: TWO letters kalit g'oyasini xaritada toping
presentation: Nega sarlavhalardan boshlayman?
Sarlavhalar topshirig'i matnni tartib bilan o'qitadi va xarita beradi. TWO letters dan boshlasangiz, matnni ikki marta o'qiysiz.
Sarlavhadagi so'z xatboshida bor. Demak shumi?
Shart emas. So'z mos kelishi — tuzoqning eng keng tarqalgan turi. Butun xatboshi shu haqidami — shuni so'rang.
Ikki sarlavha bitta xatboshiga mos keladi.
Ikkalasini ham qalam bilan yozib qo'ying va keyingi xatboshilarga o'ting. Oxirida qolgan sarlavhalarga qarab tanlaysiz.
TWO letters da javoblar tartibi muhimmi?
Yo'q. "B, E" va "E, B" bir xil. Lekin ikki javobni ikki alohida katakka yozing.
Uchta variant to'g'ridek ko'rinsa-chi?
Savolni qayta o'qing: "negative", "according to the writer", "nutritional". Bittasi matnda bor, lekin savolga tegishli emas.
Faqat bitta javobni bilsam-chi?
Ikkinchisini ham yozing — taxmin bo'lsa ham. Bo'sh katak har doim 0 ball, bitta to'g'ri harf esa 1 ball beradi.
notes: Bu darsning asosiy g'oyasi: birinchi topshiriq (sarlavhalar) ikkinchi topshiriq (TWO letters) uchun xarita bo'lib xizmat qiladi. Doskada xaritani chizing va TWO letters paytida o'quvchilardan "qaysi xatbosh?" deb so'rang.
Har sarlavha javobidan keyin so'rang: "xatboshining asosiy g'oyasi nima?" va "qaysi sarlavha tuzoq edi va nega?"
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: sarlavhalarga qaramasdan har xatboshiga o'z sarlavhasini yozish, keyin ro'yxat bilan solishtirish.
mistakes: Sarlavhani bitta so'z mosligi bo'yicha tanlash
TWO letters uchun butun matnni qayta o'qish
Matnda bor, lekin savolga tegishli bo'lmagan variantni tanlash
Teskari aytilgan variantni tanlash ("reducing the number of farm workers")
So'z mavzusi bir xil, ma'no qarama-qarshi

how: CORE — organik fermerlik va oziq-ovqat mavzusidagi asosiy so'zlar; STRONG — ilmiy maqolalardagi baholovchi so'zlar; SUPER — Passage 2 dagi akademik iboralar.
Har so'z bilan o'quvchi o'z oilasining ovqatlanishi haqida bitta gap tuzsin: "My grandmother never uses artificial fertiliser in her garden."
core: Organic vegetables are usually more expensive.
The farmer stopped using pesticides five years ago.
Fermer besh yil oldin pestitsid ishlatishni to'xtatdi.
Wheat is the main crop in this region.
An'anaviy fermerlik sun'iy kimyoviy moddalardan foydalanadi.
Organic methods often give lower yields.
Organik usullar ko'pincha kamroq hosil beradi.
Consumers want to know where their food comes from.
Iste'molchilar ovqatlari qayerdan kelishini bilishni xohlaydi.
strong: Pishirish ba'zi tabiiy toksinlarni yo'q qiladi.
The new results contradict the earlier study.
Yangi natijalar oldingi tadqiqotga zid keladi.
Carrying water by hand is inefficient.
The label on the box is misleading.
The government regulates the use of chemicals.
Hukumat kimyoviy moddalar ishlatilishini tartibga soladi.
Traces of pesticide were found in the fruit.
super: Good soil can compensate for a dry summer.
Yaxshi tuproq qurg'oqchil yozning o'rnini to'ldirishi mumkin.
Long queues are symptomatic of poor planning.
New technology brought about big changes in farming.
Yangi texnologiya fermerlikda katta o'zgarishlarni yuzaga keltirdi.
Some chefs are going back to basics with simple recipes.
Ba'zi oshpazlar oddiy retseptlar bilan asl usullarga qaytmoqda.

class_ex.title: Sarlavhalardagi kalit g'oya (SB, 3-mashq)
class_ex.instr: Har sarlavhada ma'noni o'zgartiradigan 1–2 so'zni ayting. Aynan shu so'zlar sarlavhalarni bir-biridan ajratadi.
items: i Research into whether organic food is better for us
ii Adding up the cost of organic food
iv The rich and poor see things differently
vi Testing the taste of organic food
vii Fear of science has created the organic trend
ix The need to remove hidden dangers from food
why: Xatboshida tadqiqot natijalari bo'lishi kerak — faqat fikr emas.
Xatboshida narx yoki pul haqida hisob-kitob bo'lishi kerak.
Ikki guruh solishtiriladi: boy va kambag'al davlatlar yoki odamlar.
"Taste" bitta gapda uchrashi yetmaydi — butun xatbosh ta'm sinovi haqida bo'lishi kerak.
Sabab-natija: qo'rquv → organikka qiziqish.
Ovqatdagi ko'rinmas xavf va uni yo'qotish kerakligi.
class_ex.note: O'quvchilar kalit so'zlarni belgilagach, so'rang: "ii va vi uchun xatbosh qanday bo'lishi kerak?" Ikkalasi ham oxirida ortiqcha bo'lib chiqadi — bu tafsilot tuzog'ining namunasi.

class_ex.title: Asosiy g'oya yoki tafsilot?
class_ex.instr: Ustoz qisqa xatboshini o'qiydi. O'quvchilar ikki sarlavhadan xatboshining ASOSIY g'oyasiga mosini tanlaydi.
items: 1 "Many families now buy fruit from supermarkets rather than markets. Supermarkets are open late, offer parking and accept cards. A few shoppers say the fruit tastes worse, but most value convenience above everything." A) Why shoppers choose supermarkets B) Complaints about the taste of fruit

2 "Salt has been used to keep meat and fish for thousands of years. It removes water, and bacteria cannot grow without water. Even today, some fishermen salt their catch at sea." A) Modern fishing methods B) How an old method keeps food safe

3 "School canteens in the city replaced fried food with salads last year. Pupils complained at first, and some brought sandwiches from home. By the summer, however, the number eating in the canteen had returned to normal." A) Pupils who bring their own lunch B) A change that was eventually accepted
why: Xatboshining ko'p qismi supermarket qulayliklari haqida. Ta'm — bitta gapdagi tafsilot.
Asosiy g'oya — tuz ovqatni qanday saqlashi. Baliqchilar — faqat misol.
Boshlanish (o'zgarish) → qarshilik → oxirida qabul qilish. Uydan buterbrod olib kelish — tafsilot.
class_ex.note: Har javobdan keyin so'rang: "Tuzoq sarlavha xatboshining qaysi gapiga mos keladi?" O'quvchi tuzoqni aniq ko'rsatishi kerak.

tasks.title: Questions 1–7
tasks.type: Matching headings
tasks.instr: Paragraph A — misol (viii). Qolgan B–G uchun sarlavha tanlang. Ro'yxatda 2 ta ortiqcha sarlavha bor.
items: Paragraph B
Paragraph C
Paragraph D
Paragraph E
Paragraph F
Paragraph G
answers: v A description of organic farming
i Research into whether organic food is better for us
iii The factors that can affect food quality
ix The need to remove hidden dangers from food
vii Fear of science has created the organic trend
iv The rich and poor see things differently
why: "The organic approach means farming with natural, rather than man-made, fertilisers and pesticides" — xatbosh organik fermerlik usulini tasvirlaydi (crop rotation, samarasizlik, transport).
"Studies into organic farming worldwide continue to reject this claim" + oziq-ovqat agentligining sharhi. Butun xatbosh — tadqiqotlar nima topgani.
Ovqatning foydasi yangiligi, pishirish usuli, tuproq, quyosh va yomg'irga bog'liq — sabablar ro'yxati. Tuzoq: vi — "flavour" bitta gapda, lekin ta'm sinovi haqida gap yo'q.
Ko'p oddiy ovqatlarda tabiiy toksinlar bor; "breeding out harmful traits from crops" — xavfni yo'qotish.
"It's not nature they worry about, but technology" — texnologiyadan qo'rquv organikka qiziqishni keltirib chiqargan.
Yevropa uchun "a good thing", Afrikadagi fermer uchun "a disaster" — ikki tomon turlicha ko'radi.
tasks.note: Ishlatilmagan sarlavhalar: ii "Adding up the cost" (G da "expensive luxury" bor, lekin xarajat hisoblanmaydi) va vi "Testing the taste" (D dagi "flavour of a carrot" — tafsilot tuzog'i).

tasks.title: Questions 8–13
tasks.type: Choose TWO letters, A–E
tasks.instr: Har juftlikda ikkita javob. Tartib ahamiyatsiz ("B, E" = "E, B"); imtihonda har harf alohida 1 ball. Avval kalit g'oyani belgilang, keyin sarlavhalar xaritasidan kerakli xatboshini toping. 8–9 → B xatbosh; 10–11 → D; 12–13 → E va G.
items: 8–9 Which TWO of the following points does the writer mention in connection with organic farming? A) the occasional use of pesticides B) using the same field for different crops C) testing soil quality D) reducing the number of farm workers E) the production of greenhouse gases

10–11 According to the writer, which TWO factors affect the nutritional content of food? A) who prepares the food B) the weather conditions during growth C) where the food has been stored D) when the plants were removed from the earth E) the type of farm the food was grown on

12–13 Which TWO negative aspects of organic farming does the writer mention? A) Consumers complain about the extra cost. B) Organic food may make people ill. C) Farm workers have to be specially trained. D) It requires too much technological expertise. E) It is not possible in some countries.
why: B — "crop rotation" = bir dalada navbat bilan turli ekin. E — "carbon dioxide emitted by transporting food". Tuzoqlar: C — "improve soil quality" (sinash emas); D — teskari: organik usul "inefficient in its use of labour", ya'ni ko'proq ishchi kerak; A — pestitsid tabiiy, "occasional" haqida gap yo'q.

B — "the amount of sunlight and rain crops have received". D — "freshness" va "how long ago it was dug up". Tuzoqlar: A — matnda "the way the food is cooked" (kim emas, qanday); E — organik yoki oddiy tizim farqi "likely to be greater" boshqa omillardan kichik, ya'ni ta'sir qilmaydi.

B — E xatbosh: organik ovqat xavfsizroq degan fikrga tabiiy toksinlar zid; "the closer a plant is to its natural state, the more likely it is that it will poison you". E — G: "to a farmer in rural Africa, it is a disaster", tuproqqa qaytarishga organik modda yetmaydi. Tuzoqlar: A — "expensive luxury" bor, lekin iste'molchilar shikoyati yo'q; D — teskari: G ilg'or texnologiyaga kirishni tavsiya qiladi.
tasks.note: 10–11 — eng qiyin juftlik: D xatboshida ta'm (flavour) va foyda (health value) aralash keladi. Savol "nutritional content" haqida — shuning uchun javob foyda sanalgan gaplardan olinadi.

why: Muzlatilgan sut, qalampir, suv idishi qopqog'i — ilmiy faktlar. A — sog'lom ovqatlanish maslahati yo'q; C — oziq-ovqat sanoati tanqid qilinmaydi.

answers: iv A source of information for some people
ix How certain advice is decided on
i Why a particular piece of information is given

why: "It was for such people that New Scientist developed its 'Last Word' column" — qiziquvchan odamlar uchun ma'lumot manbai.
Use-by va best-before sanalari qanday belgilanadi: "determined by its manufacturers ... lab tests and government guidelines". Sana — iste'molchiga maslahat.
"The same research explains why even bottled mineral water ... needs a best-before date" — bitta ma'lumot (sana) nega berilishi.
Yashil qalampirni quyoshda saqlamang, bananni sovutgichga qo'ymang — saqlash haqida ma'lumot.
"Years of trial and error led to ... DIN 6099" — uzoq ish natijasida xulosa: qopqoqda 21 ta tish.
"No one foodstuff that could feed the world" (hal qilinmagan muammo) + "they did come up with a menu that could feed a family of four" (yechim).
tasks.note: Ortiqcha sarlavhalar: iii "Reasons that remain a mystery" (B dagi savollarning hammasiga javob bor), vii "The need to change a system", x "Ideas not put into practice" (G ga tuzoq — lekin G da ham muammo, ham yechim bor, ii aniqroq).

tasks.title: Questions 8–13
tasks.type: Choose TWO letters, A–E
tasks.instr: Har juftlikda ikkita javob. Tartib ahamiyatsiz ("B, E" = "E, B"); imtihonda har harf alohida 1 ball. Avval kalit g'oyani belgilang, keyin sarlavhalar xaritasidan kerakli xatboshini toping.
items: 8–9 Which TWO of the following are explained by the writer in the text? A) why the 'Last Word' column was created B) why use-by dates are more important than sell-by dates C) how to prevent bacteria getting into bottled water D) a way in which peppers are similar to bananas E) why most bottle caps have a common feature

10–11 Which TWO problems connected with food does the writer mention? A) confusing information about the use of pesticides B) feeling pain when eating something C) sell-by dates sometimes being inaccurate D) feeling ill because of eating food after its best-before date E) the effect of sunlight on green peppers

12–13 Which TWO of the following would a family of four need to do to feed itself every day of the year, according to New Scientist? A) use more than one piece of land B) grow the same crop all the time C) put dead plants into the soil D) plant only crops that grow very quickly E) concentrate on crops that grow vertically
why: A — B xatbosh: ustun "such people" (qiziquvchan o'quvchilar) uchun yaratilgan. E — F: 21 tish ideal, chunki qopqoq aylanasi, metall yorilishi va mashinada tiqilib qolishi hisobga olingan. Tuzoqlar: C — suvga bakteriya qanday tushishi aytilgan, qanday oldini olish — yo'q; D — qalampir va banan farqi (biri issiqda, biri sovuqda buziladi).

B — "Why does your mouth burn for longer when you eat chillies". E — "green peppers will decay faster than red if kept in sunlight". Tuzoq: D — kasallik "use-by" sanasi bilan bog'liq; loviya "best-before" dan keyin ham yeyiladi.
C — "ploughing back dead plant matter". E — "grow vertically rather than horizontally". Tuzoqlar: A — "only eight square metres" (bitta joy); B — teskari: "rotating crops".

readings.title: Practice 1: Breakfast — the most important meal of the day?
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2 darajasi)
text: A  For generations, children have been told that breakfast is the most important meal of the day. The phrase appears on cereal boxes, in school leaflets and in countless magazine articles. Yet when scientists began to look closely at the evidence behind this familiar advice, they found that it was far less solid than most people had assumed. In fact, the popularity of the idea seems to owe at least as much to advertising as it does to nutrition science.

B  The modern breakfast is a relatively recent invention. In much of Europe before the nineteenth century, working people often ate their first proper meal in the middle of the morning, after several hours of labour. It was only with the growth of factories and fixed working hours that a meal eaten at home before leaving became normal. Food companies then helped to spread the habit even further: ready-to-eat cereals were marketed as a quick, healthy start to the day, and within a few decades they were on kitchen tables across the country.

C  For many years, the main argument for breakfast came from observational studies. These compared large groups of people and found that those who regularly ate breakfast tended to be slimmer than those who skipped it. However, such studies cannot show cause and effect. People who eat breakfast may also be more likely to exercise, sleep well and avoid smoking, and any of these habits could explain the difference in weight. In addition, people who report their own eating habits in surveys do not always remember them accurately.

D  To test the idea properly, researchers turned to controlled trials, in which volunteers are randomly told either to eat breakfast or to skip it. A review of these trials, published in a medical journal in 2019, found that breakfast eaters did not lose more weight. On average, they actually consumed slightly more calories over the whole day, because eating in the morning did not make them eat much less later on. The authors noted, however, that many of the trials were short, lasting only a few weeks, so further research is needed.

E  This does not mean that breakfast is useless. There is some evidence that children who eat in the morning concentrate better at school, particularly in the hours before lunch, although the results vary between studies. For people with diabetes, the timing of meals can matter for controlling blood sugar, and doctors may give them specific advice. Athletes who train early in the day may also perform better with some fuel in their bodies.

F  What people eat in the morning appears to matter more than whether they eat at all. Many popular breakfast foods, including some cereals, pastries and fruit juices, are high in sugar and low in fibre. They produce a rapid rise in blood sugar followed by a fall, which can leave people feeling hungry again long before lunchtime. Eggs, yoghurt, wholegrain bread and fruit, by contrast, tend to keep people full for longer. Including some protein in the first meal of the day seems to be particularly helpful.

G  For most healthy adults, then, the message from nutrition experts is surprisingly relaxed. If you are hungry in the morning, eat a sensible breakfast; if you are not, there is no strong reason to force yourself. The most useful thing people can do, experts suggest, is to pay attention to their own appetite rather than follow a rule that was partly written by the food industry. Skipping breakfast now and then is unlikely to cause any harm, as long as the rest of the day's diet is balanced.

readings.title: Practice 2: Food miles — is local always better?
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2 darajasi)
text: A  In the early 1990s, a British researcher introduced the term 'food miles' to describe the distance food travels from the farm where it is produced to the plate where it is eaten. The phrase was easy to understand, and it soon appeared regularly in newspaper articles and campaign leaflets. Some supermarkets began labelling products that had been flown in from abroad, and many shoppers came to believe that choosing food grown nearby was one of the simplest ways to help the environment.

B  The logic seems obvious. Transporting a lettuce from another continent must burn more fuel than driving it from a farm a few kilometres away. Supporters of local food also point to other benefits. Money spent at farmers' markets stays in the local economy, and fruit that does not have to survive a long journey can be picked when it is ripe, so it often has a better flavour. Many people also simply enjoy knowing the farmer who grew their food.

C  However, researchers who have measured the whole life of food products have found that transport usually accounts for only a small share of their total greenhouse gas emissions, often less than ten per cent. Far more is produced on the farm itself, through fertilisers, animal feed and, above all, the digestive processes of cattle and sheep. This means that what we eat generally matters much more than where it comes from. A kilogram of beef, for example, is responsible for many times more emissions than a kilogram of peas or beans, wherever it is produced.

D  A frequently quoted example involves tomatoes. In a cold northern country, tomatoes grown locally in winter may need heated greenhouses, which use large amounts of energy. Tomatoes grown outdoors in a warm southern country and then carried north by lorry can sometimes have a smaller carbon footprint, even though they have travelled much further. Some studies have suggested that the same may be true of lamb raised on grass in New Zealand and shipped to Britain, although the result depends on the season and the farming methods used.

E  The method of transport also makes an enormous difference. Shipping goods by sea produces very little carbon for each kilogram carried, because a single vessel can move thousands of containers at once. Air freight, on the other hand, is extremely polluting. Fortunately, only a very small proportion of food is flown, mostly fresh products that spoil quickly, such as berries, asparagus and some fish. Road transport lies somewhere in between, and short journeys in small, half-empty vans are often the least efficient of all.

F  There is also a stage that food-mile calculations often ignore: the shopper's own trip. A person who drives a long way to a farm shop to buy a small bag of vegetables may produce more emissions on that journey than the lorry that delivered hundreds of boxes to the local supermarket. Ideally, shoppers would combine several errands into one trip, or walk.

G  None of this means that local food is a bad choice. Seasonal produce from nearby farms can be fresh, tasty and good for rural communities. But experts argue that if people want to reduce the climate impact of their diet, the most effective steps are to eat less red meat and dairy and to throw away less food, rather than worrying mainly about distance. Food waste is a particularly serious issue, since all the energy used to grow, process and transport food that ends up in the bin is wasted too.

readings.title: Practice 3 (uyga): Fermented foods — an old habit returns
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2 darajasi), uy vazifasi
text: A  Long before refrigerators, people needed ways to stop food from going bad. One of the oldest solutions was fermentation, a process in which tiny organisms such as bacteria and yeasts break down the sugars in food. Archaeologists have found evidence of fermented drinks that are thousands of years old, and almost every culture has developed its own fermented foods, from yoghurt and cheese to bread, pickles and soy sauce. In Central Asia, for example, fermented milk products such as qatiq have been part of everyday meals for centuries.

B  Fermentation works partly because the organisms produce acids or alcohol as they feed. These substances make the food an unfriendly place for the harmful bacteria that cause spoilage. In cabbage pickled in salty water, for example, bacteria turn natural sugars into lactic acid, which gives the vegetable its sour taste and allows it to be stored for months. Yeasts, meanwhile, produce carbon dioxide gas, which is what makes bread dough rise.

C  In many wealthy countries, fermented foods became less common during the twentieth century. Refrigeration and industrial food processing meant there was less need for traditional methods, and many products that were once fermented slowly began to be made quickly with vinegar instead. Pickles bought in supermarkets are often heat-treated as well, which kills any living bacteria they contain. At the same time, some consumers began to associate strong, sour flavours with old-fashioned food.

D  Recently, however, interest has grown rapidly. Sales of drinks such as kombucha, a fermented tea, and kefir, a fermented milk, have risen sharply in Europe and North America, and cookery classes that teach people how to ferment vegetables at home are increasingly popular. Many restaurants now serve their own pickles, and small producers sell their products at food markets. Social media has played a part, with enthusiasts sharing photographs of their jars and recipes online.

E  Much of this enthusiasm is linked to research on the gut microbiome, the trillions of microorganisms living in the human digestive system. Scientists believe these organisms influence both digestion and the immune system. In one small study at an American university, volunteers who ate several portions of fermented food every day for ten weeks developed a more varied range of gut bacteria and showed lower levels of some markers of inflammation. Other researchers are investigating whether gut bacteria might even affect mood, although this work is at a very early stage.

F  Experts warn, though, that the evidence is still limited. Many studies have been small or short, and the effects seem to vary between different foods and different people. Some fermented products are also high in salt or sugar, and a few contain small amounts of alcohol. Claims on packaging that a product will 'boost immunity' or 'cure' digestive problems are generally not supported by strong scientific evidence. It is also unclear how many of the living bacteria in a product survive the journey through the stomach.

G  For those who wish to try fermented foods, dietitians suggest starting slowly, as a sudden increase can cause stomach discomfort. Traditional products such as natural yoghurt are inexpensive and easy to find, and adding a spoonful of pickled cabbage to a salad is a simple way to begin. Home fermenters should follow tested recipes and keep their equipment clean. People with weakened immune systems, however, should talk to a doctor before eating home-fermented foods, because mistakes in preparation can allow harmful bacteria to grow.

fermentation works partly because the organisms produce acids

a greater variety of gut bacteria

claims on packaging ... are generally not supported

intro: Section 2 — bitta so'zlovchi ijtimoiy mavzuda gapiradi: gid, rahbar, tashkilotchi. U ko'pincha ikki qismga bo'linadi: birinchisida umumiy ma'lumot (MCQ), ikkinchisida joylar yoki bino rejasi (map / plan labelling). 6.0 darajasida aynan shu juftlik eng ko'p uchraydi.

Tayyorlanish vaqtini ikkiga bo'ling. MCQ uchun: savolning SHART so'zini tagiga chizing — "why", "recommends", "most important", "advice", "asks the nurses to". Xarita uchun: qayerdan boshlanadi (main building, main entrance, reception), kompas qayerda, qanday mo'ljallar bor (roundabout, Tye Road, trees, main hall).

MCQ: uch variantning hammasi odatda eshitiladi. Debbie "gym", "heart" va "sleep" haqida gapiradi, lekin "the main advantage" deb faqat bittasini aytadi. Javob paraphrase bilan keladi: "don't lie awake at night" = "helps you sleep".

Xarita: savollar tartibi = audio tartibi. So'zlovchi sizni xarita bo'ylab "yetaklaydi": har yo'nalishdan keyin qalam bilan joyingizni belgilang. Bitta joyni yo'qotsangiz, keyingi savolda ko'rsatilgan mo'ljaldan ("go back to the main building") qayta boshlang.

Yo'nalish iboralari: opposite (qarshisida), beyond / past (o'tib), just before (sal oldin), behind (orqasida), directly in front of you (to'g'ri oldingizda), on the right-hand corner (o'ng burchakda), the second turning on the left (chapdagi ikkinchi burilish).
Chap va o'ng — yurayotgan odamniki. Agar siz xaritada pastga (janubga) qarab yursangiz, sizning chapingiz xaritada o'ngda bo'ladi. Shuning uchun kompas bo'yicha o'ylash ("to the east") xavfsizroq.
Tuzoq: so'zlovchi bir joyni aytib, keyin boshqasiga yo'naltiradi ("there's the canteen inside the main building. But I would recommend..."). Oxirgi yo'naltirilgan joy — javob.

presentation: MCQ va xarita orasida vaqt bo'ladimi?

"Left" deyildi, lekin xaritada o'ngga ketyapman.
Yurayotgan odamning chapi. Qaysi tomonga qarab yurayotganingizni tekshiring yoki kompasga tayaning.
Bitta joyni o'tkazib yubordim. Nima qilaman?
Taxminiy harf yozing va keyingisiga o'ting. Har yangi joy ko'pincha asosiy binodan qayta boshlanadi.

Map labellingda odatda yo'q. Agar ikki savolga bir harf chiqsa, bittasini qayta tekshiring.
MCQ da variantdagi so'z aynan eshitildi. Demak shumi?
Ko'pincha aksincha — aynan eshitilgan so'z tuzoq bo'ladi ("gym", "coffee", "canteen"). G'oyani tekshiring.
notes: 5.0 da MCQ va map labelling alohida o'rganilgan. Endi ular bitta Section 2 da ketma-ket: o'tish paytida xaritaga qarashga vaqt topish — asosiy ko'nikma.
Tekshiruvda xaritani ekranga chiqaring va skript bo'yicha yo'lni qalam bilan chizing. O'quvchilar har burilishda "qayerdamiz?" deb aytib boradi.
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: WB Track 3 dan keyin xaritadagi ortiqcha xonalardan (E, G) biriga o'zlari yo'l ko'rsatib gapirsin.
mistakes: Gym tilga olinadi, lekin tavsiya emas

how: CORE — sog'lom turmush va ish joyi so'zlari; STRONG — konferensiya va tashkilot so'zlari; SUPER — yo'l ko'rsatish va nutqdagi iboralar.
Har o'quvchi o'z uyidan akademiyagacha yo'lni 4–5 gap bilan tushuntiradi, kamida 3 ta yo'nalish iborasini ishlatib.
core: A balanced diet includes fruit and vegetables.
Muvozanatli ovqatlanishga meva va sabzavot kiradi.
Our supervisor showed us around the hospital.
Hygiene is very important in a hospital.
Germs can live on a desk for days.
Mikroblar stol ustida bir necha kun yashashi mumkin.
Shift work makes regular meals difficult.
The canteen is open until eight.
Take a short break every two hours.
Har ikki soatda qisqa tanaffus qiling.
The staff recreation centre has a small library.
Xodimlar dam olish markazida kichik kutubxona bor.
She takes a vitamin supplement in winter.
strong: The company started a cycling initiative.
Please complete the questionnaire before the conference.
Stress in the workplace is a common problem.
Ish joyidagi stress — keng tarqalgan muammo.
The pharmacy is opposite the bank.
The pool is just beyond the trees.
super: Don't fall into the fast-food trap.
We took your answers into account.
It's called Healthy Kitchen — the name speaks for itself.
U "Healthy Kitchen" deb ataladi — nomi o'zi aytib turibdi.
Make the most of the free sessions.

class_ex.title: Yo'nalish iboralari
class_ex.instr: Ustoz iborani o'qiydi, o'quvchilar o'zbekcha ma'nosini aytadi va doskadagi oddiy chizmada qo'li bilan ko'rsatadi.
items: directly opposite you
just beyond the line of trees
go past the turning for Tye Road
the second turning on the left
directly behind the main building
on the right-hand corner
just before you reach the roundabout
why: "Opposite" — ko'chaning yoki yo'lakning narigi tomonida, yuzma-yuz.
"Beyond" = narigi tomonida. Daraxtlar oldida emas — ulardan keyin.
"Go past" — burilmasdan o'tib ketish. Ko'p o'quvchi shu joyda buriladi — tuzoq.
Birinchi burilishni sanamang — ikkinchisi kerak.
"Behind" — asosiy kirishga nisbatan orqa tomonda (SB da back exit).
Chorraha yoki burilishdagi o'ng burchak.
"Just before" — hali yetmagan, sal oldinda.
class_ex.note: Doskaga oddiy chizma: bitta asosiy bino, bitta aylanma yo'l, bitta ko'cha va daraxtlar. Har iborada bitta o'quvchi chizmaga borib, joyni ko'rsatadi.

class_ex.title: Savoldagi shart: qaysi biri?
class_ex.instr: Ustoz gapni o'qiydi. O'quvchilar savolga javob beradi va qolgan ikki narsa nega javob emasligini aytadi.
items: "Swimming is good for your heart, and it helps with back pain, but what I like most is that it clears my head." — Main benefit for the speaker?
"You could buy a bike or join a club, but honestly, just getting off the bus one stop early is enough." — What does the speaker recommend?
"There's a café on the ground floor, but it's expensive. The staff kitchen upstairs is free and has a microwave." — Where should staff eat?
"We tried running sessions, then cooking classes. What people asked for most, though, was advice on sleep." — What was most requested?
answers: getting off the bus one stop early
why: "What I like most" — asosiy foyda. Yurak va bel — tuzoq.
"You could ... but honestly ... is enough" — "but" dan keyingi qism tavsiya.
Kafe tilga olinadi, lekin "expensive" — so'zlovchi boshqasini tavsiya qiladi.
"What people asked for most" = most requested. Birinchi ikkitasi — sinab ko'rilgan narsalar.
class_ex.note: SB Track 5 dagi 2- va 4-savol aynan shu tuzilishda: avval bir narsa aytiladi, "but" dan keyin javob.

listenings.title: Student's Book, Track 5: Debbie's talk to new nurses (Q1–5)
intro: Kasalxona rahbari Debbie Green yangi hamshiralarga ovqatlanish, jismoniy faollik, xavfsizlik va gigiyena haqida gapiradi. Tinglashdan oldin 30 soniya: har savolning shart so'zini tagiga chizing (why, recommends, most important, advice, asks).
Savollar sahifasi va xarita quyida rasm sifatida (Q6–10 xaritasi Track 6 uchun).

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Variantdagi so'zni emas, g'oyani tinglang. Uchala variant ham tilga olinishi mumkin.
items: 1 According to Debbie, why do some people fail to eat a balanced diet? A) They don't know how to cook. B) They don't have enough time to cook. C) They don't feel hungry enough to cook.
2 Debbie recommends that staff should keep fit by A) using a gym. B) taking up a new sport. C) changing some daily activities.
3 Which benefit of exercise does Debbie think is most important? A) It helps you sleep. B) It keeps your heart healthy. C) It improves mental skills.
4 What advice does Debbie give the nurses about health and safety? A) to avoid drinking coffee B) to use the canteen at night C) to take regular breaks
5 When she talks about hygiene, Debbie asks the nurses to A) wash their hands regularly. B) keep away from germs. C) help with the cleaning.
why: "It's often too easy to grab something quick, because you're tired or busy". Tuzoq: C — "when you feel hungry" eshitiladi, lekin ochlik yetishmasligi haqida emas.
"It may just be a question of doing things differently" — liftda emas, zinada. Tuzoq: A — "may not have time to join a gym"; B — "rather than starting a very active sport".
"You'll find that you don't lie awake at night ... and that's the main advantage of exercise". Tuzoq: B — yurak tilga olinadi, lekin "main advantage" emas.
"You shouldn't work for more than three hours without a break". Tuzoq: A va B — "that cup of tea or coffee in the canteen" faqat misol.

"Make sure that you don't leave even a small amount of rubbish around ... there are brooms in the cupboards, so use them". Tuzoq: A — qo'l yuvishni allaqachon bilishadi ("trained to clean your hands"); B — mikroblar tilga olinadi.
tasks.note: Kalit (SB, 44-rasm) javoblarni aynan shu iqtiboslar bilan tasdiqlaydi. 5-savolda ko'p o'quvchi A ni tanlaydi — "hands" so'zi birinchi eshitiladi.

listenings.title: Student's Book, Track 6: Map of the hospital (Q6–10)
intro: Tinglashdan oldin xaritada toping: MAIN BUILDING (start), BACK EXIT, aylanma yo'l, TYE ROAD, daraxtlar va kompas. Debbie har safar asosiy binodan boshlaydi.
SB 4-mashq: juftlikda bitta harfni tanlab, sherigingizga yo'l ko'rsating (misol: "out of the front, turn left, directly opposite you — G").

tasks.title: Questions 6–10
tasks.type: Label the map. Write the correct letter, A–H
tasks.instr: Savollar tartibi = audio tartibi. Qalam bilan yo'lni chizib boring.
items: 6 recreation centre
7 health centre
8 swimming pool and sauna
9 health-food store
10 Jenny's Restaurant
why: "Go out of the main entrance and just along the main road to the east ... It's this T-shaped building". Sharqqa — C.
"Directly behind the main hospital building. So, if you go out of the back exit, it's just in front of you" — B.

"Walk out of the front ... go down that and turn left into Tye Road — you'll see the pool entrance at the end of that road, just beyond the line of trees". Tye Road oxiri, daraxtlardan keyin — H. Tuzoq: F — Tye Road boshida.
"Go beyond the turning for Tye Road and you'll see it on the right-hand corner, directly opposite another building" — E. Tuzoq: burilishga kirmaslik kerak.

"There's always the canteen inside the main building. But I would recommend ... Jenny's Restaurant ... head for the roundabout ... take the second turning on the left ... before the trees" — A. Tuzoq: kantina.
tasks.note: Ishlatilmagan harflar: D, F, G. G — kitobdagi 4-mashq misoli ("It's G"), uni savollarga javob deb yozmang.

listenings.title: Student's Book: recording script (Track 5–6) — ustoz uchun
intro: Tekshiruvdan keyin ekranga chiqaring. Har javob gapini va tuzoq gapni alohida rang bilan ko'rsating; xaritada yo'lni skript bo'yicha chizing.

listenings.title: Workbook, Track 3: Health & Fitness in the Workplace conference (Q1–10)
listenings.qtype: Multiple choice + Plan labelling — imtihon rejimi
intro: Tashkilotchi konferensiya ishtirokchilariga dastur va bino rejasi haqida gapiradi. Avval 1-mashq: so'zlovchi qachon gapiryapti?
Keyin imtihondagidek: tayyorlanish vaqti, audio BIR MARTA. Rejada start nuqtasi — Main hall; Reception va Entrance hall ni oldindan toping.

tasks.title: 1-mashq: So'zlovchi qachon gapiryapti?
tasks.type: Choose A, B or C
tasks.instr: Ikkala topshiriqni ko'zdan kechiring va taxmin qiling, keyin audio bilan tekshiring.
items: 1 When is the speaker talking? A) at the beginning of a conference B) during the planning of a conference C) at the end of a conference
why: "Hello, and welcome to the conference" ... oxirida "OK, let's get started". Q6–10 da sessiyalar joyi so'raladi — ular hali boshlanmagan.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Savoldagi shartni belgilang: "in the past", "connection", "people attending", "in the sessions".
items: 1 The speaker says that the conference includes issues which A) were requested by participants. B) are seldom discussed. C) cause disagreement.
2 The speaker says that in the past, this subject A) caused problems in the workplace. B) was not something companies focused on. C) did not need to be addressed.
3 The speaker mentions a connection between health and fitness and A) keeping employees. B) employees' performance. C) a company's reputation.

4 What does the speaker say about the people attending the conference? A) Some of them may feel that there is not much they can learn. B) All of them have attended the conference before. C) Most of them are familiar with the speakers.
5 The speaker says that in the sessions, participants will A) work together in pairs. B) pretend to have various roles. C) describe real events.
why: "We've taken into account the answers that you gave us in our questionnaires ... the main ones that you indicated are important to you".
"Something that didn't get much attention not that many years ago" — "none of their business". Tuzoq: C — hozir kerak, oldin e'tibor berilmagan edi.
"A fit and healthy person does their job better" — ish samaradorligi. Tuzoq: "days off sick" — xodimni saqlash emas.
"Some of you may think you're already doing as much as you can ... but I promise you that you're all going to learn something new".
"In every session there will be a slot for people to talk about their own practices and experiences" — haqiqiy tajriba.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10
tasks.type: Label the plan. Write the correct letter, A–H
tasks.instr: Start — Main hall. Har yo'nalishdan keyin rejada barmog'ingizni suring.
items: 6 Setting Up a Fitness Centre
7 Healthy Eating Schemes
8 Transport Initiatives
9 Running Sports Teams
10 Conference Coordinator's Office
why: "Go out of the Main Hall here through those doors, turn right at reception and go along the corridor to the Taylor Room, which is on your left" — D.
"Go out of this hall the other way, through the doors at that end, and that takes you straight through to the Martin Suite" — H.
"Go out of those doors that bring you out opposite reception, turn left and left again into a corridor. The Fender Room is the third door on your right" — F.
"Go out of here, turn right at reception and then right again. The first door you come to on the left is the Gibson Suite" — A.
"To the left of Reception and along the corridor past the Entrance Hall ... you'll find my door at the end on your right" — C.
tasks.note: Kalit (WB, 55-rasm): 1A 2B 3B 4A 5C 6D 7H 8F 9A 10C. Ishlatilmagan xonalar: B, E, G.

listenings.title: Workbook: recording script (Track 3) — ustoz uchun
intro: Skript bilan qayta tinglashda xato qilingan savollarning gapini topishga ishlatiladi. 6–10 uchun yo'nalishlarni rejada chizib ko'rsating.

listenings.title: Jony Academy mashqi: Hillside Organic Farm — open day
intro: Ferma egasi ochiq eshiklar kunida mehmonlarga ferma haqida gapiradi va xaritani tushuntiradi. Ustoz skriptni bir marta, normal tezlikda o'qiydi.
Tinglashdan oldin xaritani doskaga chizing (pastdagi jadval: shimol — tepada). Start nuqtasi — Main barn.
transcript: SPEAKER: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Hillside Organic Farm. My name's Ruth, and my family has farmed this land for over a hundred years.

SPEAKER: People often ask how long we've been organic. We started changing about twelve years ago, but the process of conversion takes three years, so we've been fully certified organic for nine years now.

SPEAKER: And why did we change? Many visitors assume we did it for the money. It's true that organic vegetables sell at a higher price, and some of our regular customers were asking about it. But the real reason was the soil. Years of chemical fertiliser had left it hard and poor, and we wanted to bring it back to life.

SPEAKER: Now, a few things about today. Everything is free, so you don't need a ticket for anything. You're welcome to walk around the yard on your own, but if you'd like to see the fields, you'll need to join one of the guided walks, because the machinery is working out there. Boots are a good idea, but they're not essential.

SPEAKER: At twelve o'clock, our chef, Anna, will give a cooking demonstration. Last year she did bread-making, which was very popular, and a lot of you asked about cooking with children – we're planning that for next month. Today, though, she'll be showing you how to make the most of the vegetables that are in season right now: pumpkins, squash and beans.

SPEAKER: And one more thing. We opened our café two years ago, and we've always run composting days for local gardeners. But this year, for the first time, we're delivering weekly boxes of vegetables to homes in the town. There are leaflets about that at the shop.

SPEAKER: Right, let's look at the map. We're here, in the main barn, in the middle of the farm. Right next door to this barn, on its east side, is the farm shop. Please don't confuse it with the building further south on the same side, next to the yard – that's our packing shed, and it's closed to visitors.

SPEAKER: If you walk north from the barn, you'll come to the pond. The compost area is on the far side of the pond, to the west – in the north-west corner. The building on the eastern side of the pond is where we keep the beehives, so please keep away from that one.

SPEAKER: The hens used to live in the building on the west side of the main yard, but last spring we moved them to the south-west corner, right beside the main gate, where they have much more space. You can buy food for them at the shop.
SPEAKER: And that old hen house on the west side of the yard? It's now our café, so do go and try the soup.

SPEAKER: Finally, if anyone feels unwell, the first aid room is on the east side of the main gate, next to the car park. The toilets, by the way, are just beside this barn, on its west side. OK, enjoy your visit!

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Savoldagi shart so'zini belgilang: fully, main reason, must do, focus, new this year.
items: 1 How long has the farm been fully organic? A) three years B) nine years C) twelve years
2 What was the main reason the family changed to organic farming? A) Customers asked them to. B) They wanted to improve the soil. C) They wanted to earn more money.
3 What must visitors do if they want to see the fields? A) buy a ticket B) join a guided walk C) wear boots
4 Today's cooking demonstration will focus on A) using vegetables that are in season. B) baking bread. C) cooking with children.
5 What is new at the farm this year? A) a vegetable delivery service B) a café C) composting days
why: "We've been fully certified organic for nine years now". Tuzoq: 12 — o'zgarish boshlangan vaqt; 3 — o'tish davri.
"But the real reason was the soil". Tuzoq: A va C — "some customers were asking", "higher price" — lekin "but" dan keyin asl sabab.
"If you'd like to see the fields, you'll need to join one of the guided walks". Tuzoq: A — "you don't need a ticket"; C — "not essential".
"Today ... how to make the most of the vegetables that are in season right now". Tuzoq: B — o'tgan yil; C — keyingi oy.
"This year, for the first time, we're delivering weekly boxes of vegetables". Tuzoq: B — ikki yil oldin; C — "always".

tasks.title: Questions 6–10 — Hillside Organic Farm (xarita)
tasks.type: Label the map. Write the correct letter, A–H
tasks.instr: Jadval — xarita: shimol tepada, g'arb chapda. Start — Main barn. Har joy uchun harf yozing.
items: 6 Farm shop
7 Compost area
8 Hen house
9 Café
10 First aid room
why: "Right next door to this barn, on its east side, is the farm shop" — D. Tuzoq: F — "further south on the same side" — packing shed.
"On the far side of the pond, to the west – in the north-west corner" — A. Tuzoq: B — asalari uyalari.
"We moved them to the south-west corner, right beside the main gate" — G. Tuzoq: E — tovuqlar ILGARI shu yerda edi.
"That old hen house on the west side of the yard? It's now our café" — E.
"The first aid room is on the east side of the main gate, next to the car park" — H. Tuzoq: C — hojatxona ("beside this barn, on its west side").
tasks.note: 8- va 9-savol — eng yaxshi tuzoq namunasi: E harfi 8-savolda tuzoq, 9-savolda javob. O'quvchilarga "used to" iborasiga e'tibor berishni ayting.

Centre
East

homework_intro: Bugun Section 2 da ikki savol turini ketma-ket yechdik: avval MCQ, keyin xarita. Eng ko'p ball ikki joyda yo'qoladi — MCQ dagi "eshitilgan so'z" tuzog'i va xaritada yo'nalishni yo'qotish.

Birinchi vazifa — shadowing: SB Track 6 ni (xarita qismi) skript bilan birga 3 marta tinglang va so'zlovchi bilan bir vaqtda takrorlang. Oxirgi marta o'zingizni yozib oling va ovozli xabarni guruhga yuboring.

Ikkinchi vazifa — diktant: WB Track 3 ning ikkinchi qismini ("OK, now let's move on...") tinglang va 5 ta yo'nalish gapini to'liq yozib oling. Keyin skript bilan solishtiring va xatolarni qizil rang bilan belgilang.

Uchinchi vazifa — o'z xaritangiz: uyingiz yoki mahallangiz xaritasini chizing, 3 ta joyni harf bilan belgilang va 1 daqiqalik ovozli xabarda har biriga yo'l ko'rsating (opposite, beyond, turn left/right, the second turning). Sherigingiz eshitib, harflarni topadi.

homework.title: Shadowing: SB Track 6
homework.instr: Skript bilan 3 marta tinglash va takrorlash; oxirgisini yozib, guruhga yuborish.
homework.answers: Ustoz talaffuz va urg'uni tekshiradi (opposite, beyond, roundabout).

homework.title: Diktant: WB Track 3 (2-qism)
homework.instr: 5 ta yo'nalish gapini to'liq yozish, skript bilan solishtirish.
homework.answers: Skript rasmi bilan tekshiriladi; xatolar xatolar daftariga.

homework.title: O'z xaritangiz: ovozli yo'l ko'rsatish
homework.instr: Xarita + 3 joy + 1 daqiqalik ovozli xabar; sherik harflarni topadi.

lessons.title: Unit 3 Reading — Passage 3: Yes / No / Not Given + Summary (word list) + Multiple choice
lessons.grammar_topic: Passage 3 kombinatsiyasi: YES / NO / NOT GIVEN + Summary completion (so'zlar ro'yxati) + Multiple choice (A–D)
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 3 (Getting the message across) — til o'rganish, muloqot, yozuv uslubi
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 5–6.5: Student's Book, Unit 3, 30–32-betlar (Reading Section 3); Workbook, Unit 3, 20–22-betlar. Practice 1–3 — Jony Academy matnlari.
objectives: Passage 3 da uch savol turi kelganda har guruhni matnning qaysi qismiga tegishli ekanini 1–2 daqiqada aniqlash (xarita usuli).
YES / NO / NOT GIVEN da faktni emas, YOZUVCHINING FIKRI va da'vosini tekshirish; T/F/NG bilan farqini tushunish.
Summary sarlavhasidan matndagi kerakli xatboshini topish va ro'yxatdagi variantlarni so'z turi va ma'nosi bo'yicha qisqartirish.
MCQ (A–D) da savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oya bo'yicha joyni topish va "xatboshining maqsadi" savollariga javob berish.
Uch tur uchun 20 daqiqani to'g'ri taqsimlash: YNNG → summary → MCQ (yoki kitobdagi tartib bo'yicha).
materials: Student's Book, Unit 3, 30–32-betlar ("Why don't babies talk like adults?") — sinfda birga ishlanadi.
Workbook, Unit 3, 20–22-betlar ("Strictly English") — mustaqil mashq.
Practice 1–3 matnlari chop etilgan varaqlar (har o'quvchiga) — pastdagi Reading bo'limidan.
Taymer: Passage 3 uchun 20 daqiqa normasi doskaga yoziladi.
Doskada uch ustun: "YNNG → qaysi xatboshilar?", "Summary → sarlavha qaysi qismga?", "MCQ → kalit g'oya".

Uch savol turi birga
Ustoz doskada: xarita usuli; YNNG — yozuvchi fikri; summary + so'zlar ro'yxati; MCQ A–D; vaqt taqsimoti; tuzoqlar.
Sinf mashqi
Mini-matn bo'yicha YES/NO/NOT GIVEN va SB summary bo'shliqlari uchun so'z turini aniqlab, variantlarni qisqartirish.

Q1–14 birga ishlanadi: har javob uchun isbot gap va paraphrase juftligi.

20 daqiqa mustaqil (imtihon rejimi), keyin javoblar izoh bilan tekshiriladi.
Practice 1
"Talking with our hands" — 18 daqiqa vaqt bilan, keyin qisqa tahlil.
Practice 2

Xulosa va vazifa
Practice 3 va 30-Day Reading Challenge (Day 30, Day 18) uyga; xatolar daftari.

intro: Passage 3 — imtihondagi eng uzun va eng qiyin matn. Unda faqat ma'lumot emas, yozuvchining FIKRI va dalillari ham bo'ladi. Shuning uchun Passage 3 da ko'pincha YES / NO / NOT GIVEN keladi, 14 ta savol esa odatda uch guruhga bo'linadi: bu darsda YNNG (1–4), summary + so'zlar ro'yxati (5–9) va multiple choice A–D (10–14).

Birinchi qadam — XARITA (1–2 daqiqa). Uchala guruhga ko'z yugurting: YNNG kalit so'zlari (babytalk, Behaviourists, one-word sentences), summary sarlavhasi ("Two theories about babytalk") va MCQ dagi ismlar/raqamlar (Snedeker, Harvard, "critical period", "seventh paragraph"). Har guruh matnning qaysi qismiga tegishli ekanini chetga yozib qo'ying.

YES / NO / NOT GIVEN — T/F/NG ning "fikr" versiyasi. Savol: "Yozuvchi shunday deydimi yoki shunday o'ylaydimi?" YES — yozuvchi rozi; NO — yozuvchi aksini aytadi; NOT GIVEN — yozuvchining bu masaladagi fikri matnda yo'q. Savollar matn tartibida keladi.

Summary + so'zlar ro'yxati (A–H): javob matndan ko'chirilmaydi — ro'yxatdagi HARF yoziladi. Ro'yxatda variantlar bo'shliqlardan ko'p (5 bo'shliq, 8 variant), ya'ni 3 ta ortiqcha. Ro'yxatdagi so'zlar ko'pincha matndagi so'zning paraphrase'i bo'ladi: "walk" → physical movement, "multiply/add" → mathematical knowledge.

Variantlarni qisqartirish: avval har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini aniqlang (ot, sifat, ot birikmasi), keyin grammatik jihatdan mos kelmaydiganlarini chiqarib tashlang. Qolgan 2–3 variant orasidan matndagi ma'no bo'yicha tanlang. Summary tartibi odatda matn tartibiga mos, lekin summary faqat bir-ikki xatboshini qamrashi mumkin.

MCQ (A–D): savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyani tagiga chizing va joyni toping. "What is the writer's main purpose in the seventh paragraph?" — butun xatboshining VAZIFASI so'raladi, bitta detal emas. Noto'g'ri variantlarda ko'pincha matndagi so'zlar bor, lekin ma'no boshqa ("China" → "English lessons in China").

Vaqt: Passage 3 ga 20 daqiqa. Taxminan: xarita 2 daqiqa, YNNG 5–6, summary 5–6, MCQ 6–7 daqiqa. Kitobdagi tartib har doim bir xil emas (30-Day Challenge Day 30 da MCQ → summary → YNNG) — xarita har doim birinchi.
formulas: extremely amused = few things are as funny
So'z bir xil ≠ ma'no bir xil

Yo'q. So'zlar ro'yxati berilgan bo'lsa, faqat HARF yoziladi (C, F ...).

class_ex.title: Yozuvchi nima deydi? — mini-matn
class_ex.instr: Ustoz doskaga yozadi: "Many parents believe that watching cartoons in English will make their children fluent. I doubt it. Children certainly pick up some words and phrases this way, but real fluency requires conversation, not just listening." Har gap uchun javob va isbotni ayting.
items: Children can learn some English words from cartoons.
Cartoons are the best way to become fluent in a language.
Most parents in Uzbekistan let their children watch cartoons in English.
Listening on its own is enough to become fluent.
why: "Children certainly pick up some words and phrases this way". "Certainly" — yozuvchi rozi.
"I doubt it" — yozuvchi ota-onalar fikriga qo'shilmaydi.
Ota-onalar fikri bor, lekin qaysi davlatda va nechta ota-ona ekani haqida yozuvchi hech narsa demaydi.
"Real fluency requires conversation, not just listening" — teskari.
class_ex.note: 1- va 2-gapni solishtiring: ikkalasi ham multfilm haqida, lekin yozuvchi birinchisiga rozi, ikkinchisiga qarshi. YNNG da aynan shu nozik farq tekshiriladi.

class_ex.title: So'z turi → variantlarni qisqartirish (SB, 6–7-mashq)

why: "Few things are as funny as a baby who talks like an adult". "Extremely amused" = "few things are as funny".

6 ... in the same way that it does to master other abilities such as (6).

9 Children's (9) develops in the same way.

"Children don't learn to walk until their bodies are ready". Walk = physical movement. Tuzoq: E — bu ikkinchi nazariyaning misoli.

"Don't usually begin speaking in two-word sentences until they've learned a certain number of single words" — so'zlar soni, ya'ni lug'at darajasi. Keyingi xatboshi ham buni tasdiqlaydi: "what matters is ... the number of words you know".

"Children learn to multiply after they have learned to add" — matematika ham bosqichma-bosqich.
